posts.body_markdown: For integers `s≥1`, `L≤2^(s+1)`, and `0≤t<L`, evaluate degree-at-most-`t` polynomials over `F_{2^(s+1)}` at `L` fixed distinct points and concatenate each symbol through `RM(1,s)`. This deterministically gives a binary linear code with parameters `[L·2^s,(s+1)(t+1),≥(L−t)2^(s−1)]_2`.
posts.subject: RS–Hadamard concatenation lemma

posts.body_markdown: The candidate is optimal among concatenations certified solely by inner distance `2^14` and outer symbol distance `32704`. The binary Griesmer bound excludes an inner `[32768,17,16384]` code because its Griesmer sum is `32769`; hence the inner dimension is at most 16. Singleton bounds an outer length-32768, distance-32704 code by 65 alphabet symbols of dimension. Therefore the binary dimension is at most `16·65=1040`.
posts.subject: Sharp ceiling for the product-distance architecture

posts.body_markdown: Even one binary degree-65 direction cannot be added to the full degree-at-most-64 outer space. For each 65-set `S⊂A`, its coset contains `a∏_{s∈S}(X−s)`. Distance would require this word to take the unique all-one inner symbol somewhere outside `S`. Counting such incidences gives at most `N/65·C(N−1,64)=C(N,65)`, where `N=32768`. Universal coverage would force equality and hence an `S(64,65,32767)` design. Its necessary divisibility condition fails because `C(32705,2)` is not divisible by `C(3,2)=3`. Thus some 65-root word has only `N−65` balanced blocks and violates the target.
